 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Portland Trail Blazers are on the road Tuesday night as they travel to take on the Los Angeles Lakers in a Western Conference showdown.
 Portland enters Tuesday's game with a 2-0 record after defeating the Sacramento Kings on the road Friday night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Portland Trail Blazers forward Deni Avdija (8)© Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images
 In Friday's victory, Deni Avdija led the way for the Trail Blazers as he recorded 26 points, seven rebounds and six assists while Damian Lillard added 19 points and five rebounds of his own.
 The Trail Blazers will try to grab another victory Tuesday as they face off against the Lakers in a tough road matchup.
 Los Angeles enters Tuesday's contest with a 3-0 record after defeating the Utah Jazz on the road Sunday night.
 Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77)Kirby Lee-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect
 Luka Doncic led the way for the Lakers in Sunday's victory as he ended the game with 52 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists while Austin Reaves recorded 29 points and four assists.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While both teams are looking to pick up a victory in Tuesday night's matchup, one may be without multiple key players due to injuries.
 Trail Blazers Injury Report: Will Scoot Henderson Play?
 Portland Trail Blazers guard Scoot Henderson (0)Scott Wachter-Imagn Images
 The Trail Blazers have three players listed on their injury report, including guard Scoot Henderson.
 Portland has listed Henderson as questionable due to left ankle soreness and he is in danger of missing his first game of the season.
 If Henderson is sidelined, Jrue Holiday and Vit Krejci could both be in line for increased roles off the bench behind Lillard and Ja Morant.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Trail Blazers have also listed Branden Carlson as questionable due to a concussion while Shaedon Sharpe has been ruled out as he continues to recover from right meniscus surgery.
 Lakers Injury Report
 The Lakers have two players listed on their injury report as they have ruled out Cameron Carr due to a right oblique strain and Adou Thiero due to a left knee effusion.
 Fans can catch Tuesday night's matchup between the Trail Blazers and Lakers from Crypto.com Arena at 11 p.m. ET on Peacock in most of the country and on NBC in the Pacific time zone.
